items.stem:
Translate the following statement into a balanced chemical equation.
“When barium chloride reacts with aluminium sulphate, aluminium chloride and barium sulphate are formed.”
State the type of this reaction giving reason to justify your answer.
items.answer:
3BaCl₂(aq) + Al₂(SO₄)₃(aq) → 2AlCl₃(aq) + 3BaSO₄(s)
This reaction is an example of a double displacement (precipitation) reaction. Since an exchange of ions takes place between both the reactants leading to the formation of a precipitate, it is an example of a double displacement (precipitation) reaction.
items.ocr: MinerU dropped the reaction arrow from the LaTeX block; restored → between reactants and products.

items.stem:
State whether the given chemical reaction is a redox reaction or not. Justify your answer.
MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂
items.answer:
The reaction given in the question is an example of a redox reaction because oxidation and reduction are taking place simultaneously in the reaction.
(i) MnO₂ + 4H⁺ + 2e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 2H₂O
In the above reaction MnO₂ is converted to Mn²⁺ because addition of electrons takes place, hence MnO₂ is the compound which is reduced.
(ii) 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻
In the above reaction Cl⁻ is oxidised to Cl₂ because removal of electrons takes place. Hence the compound which is oxidised is HCl.

items.stem: What is a chemical equation? Illustrate with an example.
items.answer:
The mode of communicating facts in chemical language about a chemical reaction is called a chemical equation. For example, the reaction of zinc with dilute sulphuric acid to produce zinc sulphate and hydrogen is given by the following chemical equation:
Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂

items.stem: What do you understand by skeletal and balanced chemical equation?
items.answer:
If the number of atoms of any element in a chemical equation is not equal on both sides, it is called a skeletal equation. For example,
Mg + HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂
In a balanced equation, the number of atoms of different elements on both sides of a chemical equation are equal. For example,
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂

items.stem: What are the essentials of a chemical equation?
items.answer:
(i) It must refer to an actual chemical reaction.
(ii) It should be molecular. For example, H, O, N should be written as H₂, O₂, N₂.
(iii) It should be balanced and conform to the law of conservation of matter.

items.stem: Explain electrolytic decomposition with suitable examples.
items.answer:
When electricity is passed through a molten compound which is ionic in nature, then the ions of the compound separate into components, decomposing the compound. Example:
2H₂O(l) —Electricity→ 2H₂(g) + O₂(g)
This is an example of electrolytic decomposition since a compound is decomposed by passing electricity through it.

items.stem: When ferrous sulphate is heated, the green colour of ferrous sulphate changes to brown due to the formation of ferric oxide, with a smell of burning sulphur. Explain the reaction.
items.answer:
The given reaction can be represented as:
2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂↑ + SO₃↑
(ferrous sulphate, green) → (ferric oxide, brown) + sulphur dioxide + sulphur trioxide
Since ferrous sulphate is decomposed, on heating, into ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide, this is a thermal decomposition reaction.

items.stem:
Consider the following displacement reactions:
(i) CuSO₄(aq) + Fe(s) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)
(ii) FeSO₄(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Fe(s)
State which is the most reactive and which is the least reactive metal out of zinc, copper and iron.
items.answer:
(i) In the first reaction, iron displaces Cu from CuSO₄ solution, so iron is more reactive than copper.
(ii) In the second reaction, zinc displaces iron from its sulphate solution, so zinc is more reactive than iron.
Thus, zinc is more reactive than iron which is more reactive than copper. Therefore zinc is the most reactive and copper is the least reactive metal.

items.stem: What are oxidation reactions?
items.answer:
It is a process in which (a) oxygen or any electronegative element is added up, or (b) hydrogen or any electropositive element is removed, or (c) electrons are released. Examples are:
(a) Sulphur burns in air with a blue flame to form sulphur dioxide. Oxygen is added to sulphur.
S(s) + O₂(g) → SO₂(g)  (addition of oxygen to sulphur)
(b) Hydrogen sulphide combines with iodine to give hydrogen iodide and sulphur.
H₂S + I₂ → 2HI + S  (removal of hydrogen from H₂S)
(c) Sodium atom ionises to give Na⁺ ions.
Na → Na⁺ + e⁻  (release of electron)

items.stem: A thin zinc plate was kept in a glass container having CuSO₄ solution. On examining it was found that the blue colour of the solution is getting lighter and lighter. items.stem: Aluminium is a reactive metal but is still used for packing food articles. Why?
items.answer: Aluminium is quite reactive; when it is kept in air or oxygen for some time, the upper surface gets converted into its oxide called aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃), which gets deposited as a thin coating on the surface of the metal. This aluminium oxide is passive. Therefore, the metal is used for packing food articles, which do not get spoiled in the foil.

items.stem: Give one example of a redox reaction which is also a displacement reaction.
items.answer:

The reaction of zinc oxide with carbon is a redox reaction as well as a displacement reaction. It is a redox reaction because zinc oxide is reduced to zinc (by losing oxygen) whereas carbon is oxidised to carbon monoxide (by gaining oxygen). It is a displacement reaction because carbon is displacing zinc from zinc oxide to form zinc metal and CO.

items.stem: Define a chemical equation. What is an unbalanced equation called? What law covers the balancing of a chemical equation? State it.
items.answer: A chemical equation is a shorthand representation of a chemical reaction using the symbols and formulae of the substances involved in the reaction. An unbalanced chemical equation is called a skeletal chemical equation. The law of conservation of mass governs the balancing of a chemical equation. It states that “mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.”

items.stem:
Reverse of the following chemical reaction is not possible:
Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)
Justify this statement with reason.
items.answer:
Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)
The reverse of the above reaction is not possible because Cu is less reactive than Zn. So, it cannot displace Zn from its salt solution.

items.stem:
(a) Why is combustion reaction an oxidation reaction?
(b) How will you test whether the gas evolved in a reaction is hydrogen?
items.answer:
(a) A combustion reaction is an oxidation reaction because it is always carried out in the presence of air or oxygen.

items.stem: You must have tasted or smelt the fat and oil containing food materials left for a long time. Such foods taste and smell bad. What is the reason for this, and the name given to the phenomenon? List two measures taken at home to prevent it.
items.answer:
It happens due to oxidation of the fatty matter contained in the food, and this phenomenon is known as rancidity.
Measures of prevention:
(i) Keeping such food materials in air-tight containers.
(ii) Refrigeration of such food materials.

items.stem: Write two examples of every day life, where redox reactions are taking place.
items.answer:
(i) Silver jewellery tarnishes due to the reaction of H₂S gas in the air, in which silver is oxidised to silver sulphide.
(ii) In the rusting of iron, iron is oxidised to iron oxide.

items.stem: Food items can be preserved for longer time when kept in a refrigerator. What is the reason behind this fact?
items.answer: At lower temperature, the oxidation process of the food items gets slowed down. Hence, these food items can be preserved for a longer time.

items.stem: A student has been collecting silver coins and copper coins. One day she observed a black coating on copper coins. Which chemical phenomenon is responsible for these coatings? Write the chemical name of black and green coatings.
items.answer: The phenomenon responsible for these coatings is corrosion. Silver gets a black coating of silver sulphide when it reacts with hydrogen sulphide in the air. Copper gets a green coating of copper carbonate when it reacts with moist carbon dioxide in the air.
